account: Baker Hughes (incl. Cordant / Leucipa digital software)

snapshot.fact: FY2025 revenue $27.733B (flat vs $27.829B in 2024); OFSE $14.324B (-8% YoY), IET $13.409B (+10% YoY); FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA $4.825B; record FY2025 free cash flow $2.7B.
Approximately 56,000 employees at Dec 31, 2025, more than 45,000 of them outside the U.S.

Segments: Oilfield Services & Equipment (Well Construction; Completions, Intervention & Measurements; Production Solutions; Subsea & Surface Pressure Systems) and Industrial & Energy Technology (Gas Tech Equipment; Gas Tech Services; Industrial Products; Industrial Solutions; Climate Technology Solutions). Cordant sits inside IET Industrial Solutions alongside Bently Nevada.

Chart Industries acquisition closed July 2026 and became a third operating segment (Chart FY2025 revenue $4.3B); target about $325M in annualized cost synergies within three years. Jim Apostolides leads the Chart segment and its integration.
2025 orders $29.6B (OFSE $14.7B, IET record $14.9B); RPO $35.9B at year-end 2025, of which IET backlog was $32.4B.

Q2 2026: revenue $6.742B; orders $10.5B (+49% YoY, book-to-bill 1.6); IET orders $7.088B (+101% YoY); RPO $40.1B, including a record $37.1B in IET. Horizon 2 (2026-2028) IET orders outlook raised to more than $45B.

Stated strategy: growth in LNG, FPSO, gas infrastructure and power systems; move into 'Horizon Two' with a more production-oriented, lifecycle portfolio that is less cyclical; IET margin target of 20%; OFSE roughly flat in 2026.
Power and data-center demand is a growth driver: Dynamis ordered 76 NovaLT16 turbines (~1.3 GW) for data center and O&G power; Kodiak Gas Services framework for 1 GW, with a path to 1.8 GW.

tech_posture.fact: Cordant is described as a modular, AI-enabled enterprise solution in IET Industrial Solutions that extends asset-level hardware (Bently Nevada) to full-plant offerings. Baker Hughes sells it as a commercial software product.

Microsoft MOU (Feb 2025) extends the Cordant collaboration: Cordant built with Azure AI Foundry, aligned product pipelines and joint GTM, listed in Azure Marketplace. Led on the Baker Hughes side by Aravind Yarlagadda, SVP Industrial Solutions, IET.

C3 AI joint venture renewed and expanded in May 2025, running through June 2028. Baker Hughes is also expanding internal use of C3 AI Sourcing Optimization, Inventory Optimization and Sustainability Suite.
C3 AI apps built on the C3 Agentic AI Platform integrate with Cordant for predictive maintenance, sensor health, supply chain and energy management.

Leucipa, an automated field production software launched with AWS in Jan 2023, combines physics models, ML and agentic AI. A chat interface called 'Lucy' orchestrates specialized agents with humans in the loop. Baker Hughes presented it at AWS re:Invent 2025 alongside the open-source Energy Agents project.
Repsol MOU (Oct 2024) to co-develop AI-powered automation workflows in Leucipa across Repsol's global assets.
Google Cloud collaboration announced at CERAWeek in March 2026 to develop AI-enabled power optimization and sustainability solutions for data centers.
Cordant Release 25.2.1 added hybrid AI and physics analytics and an 'AI Assistant for Work Management'.
Recent Cordant customer wins include Yara (7 facilities), CNPC Kunlun Digital and Braskem (Q4 2025); SINOPEC, Petrobras and KNPC (Q2 2026); and Basin Electric's Bison station (Q1 2026).

Has an AI & Development software team in Bengaluru (Python/Java/C++, GitHub, CI/CD, microservices, cloud and edge) working on document understanding, predictive maintenance, computer vision and robotics. Enterprise innovation centers are in Oklahoma, Houston and Mumbai.

recent_events.fact: Closed the Chart Industries acquisition in July 2026 ($13.6B per press coverage; Chart FY2025 revenue $4.3B). It is now a third segment with a target of about $325M in cost synergies within three years.
Agreed in April 2026 to sell Waygate Technologies to Hexagon for about $1.45B cash. With the transactions closed in Q1, expects about $3B in gross proceeds in 2026.
Precision Sensors & Instrumentation sold to Crane (closed Jan 1, 2026); surface pressure control business contributed to a JV with Cactus (Jan 1, 2026).
Restructuring charges: $215M in 2025 (vs $260M in 2024), $37M in Q1 2026, $11M in Q2 2026. Management repeatedly cites 'productivity and cost-out initiatives' as margin drivers.

WARN notice for 147 roles (manufacturing, engineering, purchasing, support) at the Emmott Road campus in Houston. Cuts run into spring 2027 and are attributed to market and operational pressures, consolidation and automation.
IET leadership in flux: EVP IET Ganesh Ramaswamy resigned in Oct 2025, and Maria Claudia Borras became interim EVP IET (still interim as of Feb 2026 10-K).
Rajat Seth named CIO for OFSE (Sept 2026). This suggests IT leadership is being organized by segment.
Google Cloud data-center AI collaboration announced at CERAWeek 2026.
Q3 2026 earnings are scheduled for late October 2026 (release-date notice published), so a fresh data point is coming just after this research.

agent_signals.fact: Large M&A integration (Chart) where integration explicitly covers aligning 'product and technology platforms, engineering, commercial operations and lifecycle services'. That implies application consolidation and code migration work.
Divestitures of PSI, Waygate and surface pressure control require carve-outs and TSAs. That typically means separating shared apps and data.

Ships commercial software at scale. Cordant has point releases (e.g. 25.2.1) and Leucipa runs on AWS with agent orchestration. That means a product engineering organization with real release cadence, QA and security-review load.
OT/IT convergence and legacy embedded firmware: Nozomi found 3 flaws in Bently Nevada 3500 rack incl. auth bypass; per Nozomi, no patch planned 'due to legacy limitations'.
Multi-cloud AI estate: Azure AI Foundry for Cordant, AWS for Leucipa, Google Cloud for the data-center work, and the C3 AI platform. Engineering teams are working across several stacks.

Leucipa team says agentic AI should scale customer onboarding and workflow tailoring that previously needed manual work by implementation engineers and developers, which points to a known integration/customization bottleneck.
CIO mandate explicitly includes 'solutions to improve internal productivity'. The CIO previously owned enterprise architecture, infrastructure, IT ops and cloud strategy.
Workforce reductions linked to automation, plus a sustained cost-out narrative. Pressure to do more engineering with flat or lower headcount.
Offshore engineering footprint in Bengaluru and Mumbai using GitHub and CI/CD (Python/Java/C++/Angular).

pains: HYPOTHESIS: Chart integration and three carve-outs (PSI, Waygate, SPC) create a backlog of app rationalization, ERP/PLM interface rework and data separation that SIs are billing hourly for. Devin could take on the migration and refactor tickets.

HYPOTHESIS: Cordant and Leucipa product teams must ship faster across Azure, AWS and GCP while keeping security and regression quality high. Devin could do test generation, codebase-wide security scans and dependency upgrades.
HYPOTHESIS: Customer onboarding and customization for Leucipa/Cordant (connectors, workflow tailoring) is manual engineering work that limits software revenue scale.
HYPOTHESIS: Legacy embedded and desktop software around Bently Nevada / System 1 (Windows-heavy, long-lived firmware) carries modernization and vulnerability-remediation debt.
HYPOTHESIS: The cost-out mandate means flat engineering headcount against a record IET backlog and a $45B+ Horizon 2 order target, so productivity gains must come from tooling.

openers: With Chart closed and Waygate/PSI carved out, how much of the $325M synergy plan depends on application and code consolidation, and who is doing that engineering work today: internal teams, SIs or both?

Leucipa already orchestrates agents with humans in the loop for customers. What would it take to apply the same model inside your own software delivery, for example agents handling test, security-fix and upgrade tickets for Cordant and Leucipa?

You run AI products on Azure, AWS and Google Cloud at the same time. How are you standardizing developer tooling and code security across those stacks, and where is release velocity or vulnerability backlog hurting most?
